C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-2-E18DFE92.IntentSummary:
Plan for `C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-2-E18DFE92` (tier **T1**, roadmap `RM-GOVERNED-PATH`, paying `F288`; the successor of `C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-1-A0E753F3`, supersede depth 1): **four tasks**, each carrying the narrowest instrument for its own subject, with the single full CI-equivalent verification left to `TargetAssertions` under `--assertions final --run-commands`. T-001 (prevent colliding event ids at mint: the lock-free uniqueness check and the three prevention guards), T-002 (diagnose a collided stream: the duplicate-id blocker in `recover` and the duplicate-naming refusal in `fold`; depends on T-001 because it edits the same `validateEventsAgainstAllocations`), T-003 (the `README.md` cursor-table row), and T-004 (the `bundleMinted` payer-map entry for `F288`).
**How a race is tested — two different instruments.** The **forced** collision is deterministic: T-001 adds a test-only allocation probe (the house `set*ForTests` pattern already used by `setEvaluateTargetCompleteThrowProbeForTests`, `src/grace-cursor.ts:1642`) that pins the candidate id, so a writer is made to choose an id another loose event already holds; the guard reds whenever the uniqueness check is absent or removed and greens with it, and never depends on the scheduler. The **real-concurrency** test is the probabilistic instrument: it spawns 12 real child `bun ./src/grace.ts cursor advance` processes after one `--open-epoch` and repeats **3 rounds** per guard. Three rounds at 12 concurrent writers discriminate because the unfixed writer collided in **5 of 5** measured rounds for both shapes (distinct tasks: 13 files carrying 5–8 distinct ids; same task: 12 concurrent calls leaving 5–6 files), so the chance that all three rounds happen to serialise on the unfixed tree is negligible; on the fixed tree every round is green **by construction**, not by luck. A test that could only pass when the scheduler cooperated would be worse than no test, so the real-process guard is **corroboration of the deterministic one**, never the sole evidence.
**Full-suite runs: one.** `bun run validate:ci` appears only in `TargetAssertions`, so it runs once, at `--assertions final --run-commands`; `--assertions target` is evaluated without `--run-commands`, so the same command is not executed there, and no task `Verification` runs the whole suite.
**All seven `AC-*` are close-bound** (each carries `CloseEvidence`), so no task carries `Satisfies`; absence of `Satisfies` is not an error and there is no unmapped ordinary criterion to warn.
**What the close must write, and where it is allowed (F285 / F293).** `Pays F288` is non-empty, so the close writes the record. From the engine's write loops, not from a copied list: `--flush` writes exactly four live documents (`findings.xml`, `rulings.xml`, `decisions.xml`, `registry.xml`; `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1707`), and `--retire` writes seven — those four plus the three retired siblings (`findings-retired.xml`, `rulings-retired.xml`, `registry-retired.xml`; `:1300`). The union of seven record files, the `bundleMinted` payer-map file `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, the code and docs files, and the bundle's own archive arrival are the close's write set; all of them are in `ObservedWriteScope` below **and** the seven record files plus the payer-map file are excluded from the spec's `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC`, whose exclusions were narrowed from the record directory to those seven named XML files so `plan.md` and the other ten entries stay guarded.

T-001.Title: Prevent colliding event ids at mint

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Every path that appends a loose event through `src/grace-cursor.ts` allocates an id that is unique against the loose `run/` events **and** `run-ledger.xml` and verifies that uniqueness after the write lands. When another writer already holds the candidate id, the writer removes **only the file it created in this same call** and retries with `floor = candidate + 1`; it never overwrites another writer's file, never deletes or renumbers a pre-existing event, adds **no permanent artifact** to `run/`, and introduces no lock that can leave a bundle uncloseable. The mechanism stays inside `src/grace-cursor.ts`; `src/artifact/run-membership.ts`, the loose filename schema (`<id>-<task>-<kind>.xml`), `foldEpoch`'s write→verify→delete order and `recover --fix`'s `extend-allocation` contract are unchanged.

A test-only allocation probe (house pattern `set*ForTests`, like `setEvaluateTargetCompleteThrowProbeForTests` at `src/grace-cursor.ts:1642`) pins the candidate id so the collision is **forced, not raced**. The test `forced event-id collision renumbers the writer's own file (AC-FORCED-COLLISION)` makes a writer choose an id already held by another loose event and asserts that no two events carry that id, the other writer's file is byte-identical (sha256) before and after, and the resulting stream folds; it reds when the uniqueness check is removed and greens with it.

`concurrent advances with distinct tasks yield unique event ids (AC-UNIQUE-CONCURRENT)` spawns 12 real child `bun ./src/grace.ts cursor advance` processes with 12 distinct tasks after one `--open-epoch --from 1 --to 199`, repeats that **3 rounds**, and asserts, every round, 13 event files carrying 13 distinct ids read from each file's XML `id` attribute through the shipped parser (never the filename alone). On base `b6d7abad58b36111e07129ca81f32f72504d335a` the same case yielded 13 files with **5–8** distinct ids in **5 of 5** measured rounds.

`concurrent advances on one task lose no event (AC-NO-SILENT-OVERWRITE)` spawns 12 concurrent advances on `T-001` after one open epoch, repeats **3 rounds**, and asserts 12 progress events (13 files including the opened) with no write lost. On base the same case left **5–6** files in **5 of 5** measured rounds.

`an advance does not touch a pre-existing collided stream (AC-NO-RECORDED-EVENT-TOUCHED)` builds a stream with two loose events sharing an id, then runs one more `advance`: both pre-existing files are byte-identical by sha256 before and after, the appended event carries a fresh unique id, and `ngrace cursor recover` reports the duplicate without renumbering or deleting it. This is `D41` and `cursor recover`'s stated stance as a mechanically checkable guard.

Verification.Command: bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "concurrent advances with distinct tasks"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "concurrent advances on one task"
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "does not touch a pre-existing collided stream"

T-002.Title: Diagnose a collided stream as a duplicate event id

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The fold-blocker validator (`validateEventsAgainstAllocations`, `src/grace-cursor.ts:2810`) reports a duplicated id as an issue (`duplicate event id <id> …, appears N times`), so `ngrace cursor recover` carries it in `foldBlockReasons` and `formatRecoverDiagnosis` prints `Fold: blocked (…)` on a collided stream instead of `Fold: ok`; the same reason appears in `--format json`. The duplicate check is read-only: it changes no file, renumbers nothing and deletes nothing.

`ngrace cursor fold` refuses a duplicate-id stream **before** its write loop, with a message that names the duplicated id and the duplicate-id condition — not the current `payload mismatch` text, which describes a different failure. A stream with unique ids whose payload was genuinely dropped still reports `payload mismatch`, so the existing `injectDropPayload` guards stay green and the two failures stay distinguishable.

The test `recover and fold name a duplicate event id (AC-RECOVER-NAMES-DUPLICATE)` drives both directions: a collided stream is blocked and refused with the duplicate named, and the unique-id payload-drop stream still reports `payload mismatch`. `foldEpoch`'s write→verify→delete order and `recover --fix`'s `extend-allocation` contract are unchanged.

Verification.Command: bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts -t "name a duplicate event id"

T-003.Title: Name duplicate-id diagnosis in the README cursor table

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `README.md`'s `ngrace cursor recover` row (`README.md:211`) states that recover diagnoses duplicate event ids as a fold blocker, so an operator reading the command table learns the recovery surface reports a collision rather than only allocations. No other README surface moves, and the `ngrace cursor fold` row (`:210`) stays accurate as written.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`'s `bundleMinted` map gains exactly `F288: "C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-2-E18DFE92"` — **this** successor, never the superseded `C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-1-A0E753F3` — so the walk at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2222` (`derived.get(token) === baseline[token] ?? bundleMinted[token]`) is green once the close's row makes the successor name an archive directory and `derivePayerMap` mints `F288`. `derivePayerMap` itself is unchanged.
